description: Publish a whole site from a link, as the connected user: AttachPage downloads it, so the files never pass through the conversation. Use this instead of publish_page when the site is already online as a .zip, .tar.gz or .html file, or in a public GitHub repository (github.com/owner/repo, or a /tree/branch/folder link). The download must be public https, up to 50 MB of site, 20 MB per file and 2,000 files; it is checked like an upload. A siteId replaces an existing page at the same address. Visibility is private (invitation-only, default) or public. Does not send invitations.

description.description: Optional one-line description shown in the user's pages list. An empty string clears it.

folder.description: Folder inside the download to publish, e.g. dist or site. Default: the top level, or the usual site folder (dist, build, public…) holding index.html.

project.description: Optional project to file the page under, by name or id from list_projects, e.g. "Q4 proposal". A new name starts that project. An empty string takes the page out of its project.

siteId.description: Replace this existing page at the same address.

siteName.description: Name shown to the user and recipients, e.g. "Q3 report".

slug.description: Optional address label, 3-40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. Random when omitted.

url.description: Public https link to a .zip, .tar.gz or .html file, or a GitHub repository or folder (github.com/owner/repo/tree/main/site).

visibility.description: private (invitation-only, default) or public (anyone with the link).

name: publish_from_url

folder.description: Folder of the download that was published, when not the top level.

importedFrom.description: Where the files were downloaded from.

siteId.description: Page id; pass it to replace the page later.

title: Publish from url
